reforms.description: Budget 2022 announced a review of the SR&ED (Scientific Research and Experimental Development) Program, with the stated objective of shifting away from tax-subsidies by lowering the small firm tax-credit rate toward the large firm rate, using savings to reinstate capital costs in the base for the credit and to scale up direct grants.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Rebalancing R&D tax credits toward direct grants and reinstatement of capital costs can improve allocative efficiency of innovation support and reduce deadweight loss from tax expenditures, supporting private-sector R&D productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: Budget 2022 announced a review of the SR&ED Program with stated objectives to shift away from tax-subsidies and scale up direct grants.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant reform to a major innovation instrument (SR&ED is Canada's primary R&D tax credit), with potential to reshape the balance between indirect and direct support for private-sector R&D. However, status remains at review stage, limiting current impact.
reforms.source_quote: Budget 2022 announced a review of the SR&ED Program. Small-and-medium enterprises. Shift away from tax-subsidies by lowering the small firm tax-credit rate toward the large firm rate in the Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) Program. Use the savings from this move to reinstate capital costs in the base for the credit and to scale up direct grants.
